summary: The note describes the Łódź Ghetto, also called the Litzmannstadt Ghetto, a World War II ghetto set up by Nazi German authorities in the city of Łódź for Polish Jews and Roma after the 1939 invasion of Poland. It was the second-largest ghetto in German-occupied Europe, after the Warsaw Ghetto. Originally a preliminary step toward a 'Judenfrei' Warthegau province, it became a major industrial centre producing war supplies, especially for the German Army, and its population grew with Jews deported from Third Reich territories.
one_line: A WWII Nazi ghetto in Łódź for Polish Jews and Roma that became a major war-supply industrial centre.
key_facts: The Łódź Ghetto was also known as the Litzmannstadt Ghetto, after the Nazi German name of Łódź.
It was a World War II ghetto established by Nazi German authorities for Polish Jews and Roma.
The ghetto was established following the 1939 invasion of Poland.
It was the second-largest ghetto in all of German-occupied Europe, after the Warsaw Ghetto.
The ghetto was situated in the city of Łódź.
It was originally intended as a preliminary step in a more extensive plan of creating the "Judenfrei" province of Warthegau.
The ghetto was transformed into a major industrial centre.
The ghetto manufactured war supplies for Nazi Germany and especially for the German Army.
The number of people incarcerated in the Łódź Ghetto was augmented further by Jews deported from Third Reich territories.
